Pooled result

RR 0.2081 (0.0715 to 0.6057), 95% interval

documented incident HIV infection. random-effects, estimator REML, k = 2.

τ² 0.4176 · I² 68.8% · Q 3.208 on 1 df

Read this beside the estimate. HPTN 084 (NCT03164564) ran in botswana, eswatini, kenya, malawi, south africa, uganda and zimbabwe, in cisgender women. HPTN 083 (NCT02720094) ran in argentina, brazil, peru, south africa, thailand, the united states and vietnam, in men who have sex with men and transgender women -- one african country of seven -- and it carries the larger weight in this pool. A reader taking this page as evidence about African populations is taking half of it from a trial that was mostly not African and not in women.

I-squared is 68.83% with tau-squared 0.4178. At k = 2 that statistic proves little by itself, but it does not stand by itself: the two estimates are 0.3335 (0.1785 to 0.6230) in one population and 0.1108 (0.0395 to 0.3107) in the other, and the populations differ by sex, by risk route and by region. The spread has a named cause rather than an unexplained one.

Wang et al. 2023 (PMID 37498645) report RR 0.21 (0.07 to 0.61), I-squared 70%, on 17 and 75 events. This object reports 0.2081 (0.0715 to 0.6057), I-squared 68.83%, on the same 17 and 75 events. The arithmetic here has an independent external check and it passes -- which is a statement about the computation, not about whether the two trials should have been combined.

Both registrations register grade 2 or higher adverse events as a second primary outcome. This review carries only the efficacy primary, so this page is not a benefit-and-harm summary.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

With two or three studies the Cochrane Handbook (10.10.4.4–10.10.4.5) asks for a sensitivity analysis comparing interval methods rather than a choice between them. Both are given here; the published interval is the first row.

Table 4. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
IntervalMethodSummary (95% CI)
as publishedREML0.2081 (0.0715 to 0.6057)
sensitivity (Handbook 10.10.4.5)REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)0.2081 (0.0002 to 212.2504)

The published point is 0.2081 and the house-rule point is 0.2081. The number a reader remembers does not move; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

A floor of 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never narrow an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a known problem with known handling rather than a novel judgement.

Other recorded qualifications

Statements this review records about the limits of what it establishes, which are not shown elsewhere on this page. They are reproduced from the object verbatim and are not summarised.

Table 7. Other recorded qualifications
The population difference stated on the faceThe two trials enrol different people and a reader should see that before the pooled number. HPTN 083 enrols men who have sex with men and transgender women; HPTN 084 enrols women. The intervention, the comparator and the registered primary outcome are identical, and the question -- does long-acting injectable cabotegravir prevent HIV infection better than daily oral TDF/FTC -- is the same question in both. The pool is presented as an HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis question, which is what the title asks, and not as evidence that the effect is the same in both populations. Mode of acquisition and adherence patterns differ between these groups, and k=2 cannot test whether the effect does.
What this does not establishNot that either trial is free of bias -- no risk-of-bias assessment is recorded. Not that the effect is equal in men and in women; see the population note above. Not anything about adherence, which is the mechanism most likely to drive a difference between an injectable and a daily oral regimen and is not an outcome in this pool. Not reliability of the interval at k=2 -- see Hartung-Knapp.
Heterogeneity and how it differs from the gepotidacin caseI-squared is 68.8% and tau-squared 0.418, which is substantial -- but it is heterogeneity of magnitude, not of direction, and the distinction changes what may be said. HPTN 083 gives RR 0.33 (0.18-0.62) and HPTN 084 gives RR 0.11 (0.04-0.31). Both intervals exclude 1 and both favour cabotegravir; the trials disagree about how much, not about whether. Contrast the gepotidacin topic built the same day, where one trial excluded 1 and the other did not -- there the pooled point genuinely could not be read as an answer. Here the direction is consistent and the magnitude is not established. The pooled RR 0.21 should be read as: both trials found substantially fewer infections on cabotegravir, and these two trials do not pin down the size of that difference.
The likely source of the magnitude difference not checkedThe two trials enrol different populations with different modes of HIV acquisition and, plausibly, different adherence to a daily oral comparator -- which is the arm whose performance determines the ratio. That is a hypothesis. It has not been checked against the registrations or any publication, and it is recorded as a hypothesis so that it is not mistaken later for a finding.
A only one of these two trials is an african resultRead this beside the estimate. HPTN 084 (NCT03164564) ran in botswana, eswatini, kenya, malawi, south africa, uganda and zimbabwe, in cisgender women. HPTN 083 (NCT02720094) ran in argentina, brazil, peru, south africa, thailand, the united states and vietnam, in men who have sex with men and transgender women -- one african country of seven -- and it carries the larger weight in this pool. A reader taking this page as evidence about African populations is taking half of it from a trial that was mostly not African and not in women.
C a published synthesis reproduces this number exactlyWang et al. 2023 (PMID 37498645) report RR 0.21 (0.07 to 0.61), I-squared 70%, on 17 and 75 events. This object reports 0.2081 (0.0715 to 0.6057), I-squared 68.83%, on the same 17 and 75 events. The arithmetic here has an independent external check and it passes -- which is a statement about the computation, not about whether the two trials should have been combined.
D a registered safety co primary is not carriedBoth registrations register grade 2 or higher adverse events as a second primary outcome. This review carries only the efficacy primary, so this page is not a benefit-and-harm summary.
What is not establishedThe concealment mechanism is not on the registry and no publication was read. LOW is scored on the recorded allocation, not on a mechanism nobody here has seen.
Why this is not an adjudicated disputeA blind second assessor from a different model family disagreed with this domain on 89% of judgements across 22 topics. That would ordinarily be a dispute to adjudicate. It is not one: the tool's own text names this exact evidential situation -- a bare statement that a study was randomised -- and prescribes the answer. The second assessor is not being deferred to; the guidance is being applied.
What the registry gives and does notA ClinicalTrials.gov design module records `allocation: Randomized`. It carries no sequence-generation method and no allocation-concealment mechanism. The original judgement's own note said so before scoring LOW.
How this maps to the tool s algorithmThe tool maps 'No information' on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern to a domain judgement of some concerns. This project writes NO_INFORMATION on the domain when it could not be judged from the sources read, and caps the overall at SOME_CONCERNS. Same place, and it keeps 'we could not judge this' distinguishable from 'we judged it and had concerns'.
What does not changeNo overall rating and no GRADE CERTAINTY moves. All 51 judgements were already capped at SOME_CONCERNS or HIGH by another NO_INFORMATION domain.
And it bounds a finding of oursClass 94 records assessor 2 saying NO_INFORMATION on D1/D2/D3 `100 of 100`. Measured across all 23 topics now stored that is 239 of 243, and all four exceptions are D1=SOME_CONCERNS on `agyw-hiv-prep-review` and `cab-prep-hiv-review` -- two of the three topics asked under the earlier prompt build, the one whose reply ids are bare NCTs. Under that build it is 4 of 6; under the later build 0 of 75. The 100% was measured on the later build's topics. The two-defaults mechanism stands; its universality does not, and what varies with it is the prompt.
The rate is still conditional on the same allow listBoth numbers are conditional on the fact list in THE_ALLOW_LIST_THE_RATE_IS_CONDITIONAL_ON above. Neither is a rate of agreement between assessors in general.
ScopeHIV-1 infection under CAB-LA versus tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-emtricitabine, plus safety and treatment outcomes not comparable to this object
The finding of this comparisonThe closest agreement with a published synthesis anywhere in this corpus. Wang et al., jmir Public Health and Surveillance 2023, PMID 37498645, report CAB-LA versus TDF/FTC for prevention as RR 0.21 (95% CI 0.07 to 0.61), I-squared 70%, on 17 events of 5,161 against 75 of 5,129. This object reports RR 0.2081 (0.0715 to 0.6057), I-squared 68.83%, on 13 + 4 = 17 events against 39 + 36 = 75. The event counts are the same numbers. The one place the two differ. They pool 5,161 and 5,129 participants; this object pools 3,894 and 3,891 -- about 1,250 more per arm on their side, contributing no events. Nothing read explains where those participants come from; the candidates are a wider analysis population on the same two trials, or a further prevention trial with zero infections. Which it is has not been established and no included-study table was opened. Their review states twelve trials -- seven of them prevention trials -- against this object's two. On the stated count alone that is the largest gap in the corpus. Yet the contrast itself rests on the same seventeen and seventy-five events. A stated trial count and the evidence contributing to a particular contrast are different things, and this topic is the proof. It is why class 82 reports 'ours lower' and 'trials identified' as separate states, and why the four count-only topics are worded as a difference in stated counts and nothing more. What the agreement does not certify is that the pool is a good idea. The two trials are in different populations across different regions and I-squared is 68.83%. A second team reaching the same number from the same events does not make the combination appropriate -- it makes the arithmetic checked. GRADE certainty here is LOW and indirectness is rated down.

Abstract

Question. In Long-acting injectable cabotegravir versus daily oral TDF/FTC for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis, what is the effect on versus daily oral TDF/FTC on documented incident HIV infection?1

Methods. estimates were pooled under a random-effects with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.2

Results. Documented incident HIV infection: risk ratio 0.208 (0.0715 to 0.606) across 2 trials; 1 of these pooled outcome(s) carries a stated qualification -- a referral or a recorded finding -- given in full in Results and not reproduced here; the trials agreed loosely (I-squared 68.8%); and certainty of the evidence was low.3

Introduction

1Background. This review asks: In Long-acting injectable cabotegravir versus daily oral TDF/FTC for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis, what is the effect on versus daily oral TDF/FTC on documented incident HIV infection? It pools 2 randomised trials, against daily oral TDF/FTC. The outcome pooled is documented incident HIV infection. Every count and denominator behind those estimates is read as follows. Registry throughout. Every count and denominator is read from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results. No publication figure is used.

[Draft] The evidence identified on this question is 2 randomised trials (NCT02720094, NCT03164564), pooled here at 0.208 (95% CI 0.071 to 0.606) for documented incident HIV infection. Certainty in that estimate is rated LOW, rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness and imprecision. What this estimate does not establish is recorded in full with the result in Results, and is not restated here. Which of those unresolved points makes the question worth asking now is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] A search for published syntheses matched 46 record(s); 46 were read and 1 appraised against this review. The appraised synthesis is Safety and Efficacy of Long-Acting Injectable Agents for HIV-1: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (jmir Public Health and Surveillance, 2023). Whether those differences warrant a new synthesis rather than citing the existing one is the author's judgement.3

Methods — synthesis

For documented incident HIV infection, a random-effects model was fitted with the REML estimator.1

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) (), following . 2 result-level assessments were made.2

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.3

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons., following . 0 pooled outcome(s) were rated. 1 outcome(s) were not rated because their pool is declined or withdrawn: there is no effect estimate to rate the certainty of, and rating one would be certainty about a number this review refused to publish.4

Results

The pooled risk ratio for documented incident HIV infection was 0.208 (0.0715 to 0.606) across 2 trials, against daily oral TDF/FTC.1

Noted on this pool. Read this beside the estimate. HPTN 084 (NCT03164564) ran in botswana, eswatini, kenya, malawi, south africa, uganda and zimbabwe, in cisgender women. HPTN 083 (NCT02720094) ran in argentina, brazil, peru, south africa, thailand, the united states and vietnam, in men who have sex with men and transgender women -- one african country of seven -- and it carries the larger weight in this pool. A reader taking this page as evidence about African populations is taking half of it from a trial that was mostly not African and not in women. I-squared is 68.83% with tau-squared 0.4178. At k = 2 that statistic proves little by itself, but it does not stand by itself: the two estimates are 0.3335 (0.1785 to 0.6230) in one population and 0.1108 (0.0395 to 0.3107) in the other, and the populations differ by sex, by risk route and by region. The spread has a named cause rather than an unexplained one. Wang et al. 2023 (PMID 37498645) report RR 0.21 (0.07 to 0.61), I-squared 70%, on 17 and 75 events. This object reports 0.2081 (0.0715 to 0.6057), I-squared 68.83%, on the same 17 and 75 events. The arithmetic here has an independent external check and it passes -- which is a statement about the computation, not about whether the two trials should have been combined. Both registrations register grade 2 or higher adverse events as a second primary outcome. This review carries only the efficacy primary, so this page is not a benefit-and-harm summary.2

The trials' results were loosely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 68.8%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0.418, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 3.21, on degrees of freedom 1.3

What this does not establish: Not that either trial is free of bias -- no risk-of-bias assessment is recorded. Not that the effect is equal in men and in women; see the population note above. Not anything about adherence, which is the mechanism most likely to drive a difference between an injectable and a daily oral regimen and is not an outcome in this pool. Not reliability of the interval at k=2 -- see Hartung-Knapp.4

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials). The unit of assessment is a result1

A domain that cannot be judged from the sources read is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect. Overall is capped at SOME_CONCERNS wherever a domain is NO_INFORMATION.2

A second, independent assessment was obtained from: gpt-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`3

The assessment above was made by: Claude Opus 5 (anthropic family)4

How the second assessor was asked: Blind. Given the registration facts and the house NO_INFORMATION-never-LOW rule inline, asked to score five domains and an overall per result. Not shown this assessment and not asked whether it agreed. Asking 'do you agree' measures deference, not judgement.5

The disagreement rate, reported as disagreement because agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing: 2 of 12 judgements on this topic -- 16.7%. Both are D1 and nothing else. D2, D3, D4, D5 and the overall all agree.6

Where they disagree: Assessor 1 scored D1 = LOW on the strength of the registry recording `allocation: Randomized`. Assessor 2 scored SOME_CONCERNS. The rob 2 guidance settles it and against assessor 1: Box 4, signalling question 1.1, says verbatim 'Answer No information if the only information about randomization methods is a statement that the study is randomized', and section 4.4 says 'A judgement of low risk of bias requires that the trial has an adequate method of concealing the allocation sequence'. No concealment method was read on any trial here. Assessor 2 is also right about the level: No-information on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern maps to some concerns, which is what it returned.7

What has not been changed on the strength of it: The 51 D1 = LOW judgements across 15 topics are with Mahmood as a methodological decision. Measured consequence if they all move: Zero overall ratings change and zero GRADE ratings move, because all 51 already sit under SOME_CONCERNS or HIGH on another NO_INFORMATION domain.8

Where they disagree, by domain: D1 2 of 2 disagree, D2 0 of 2 disagree, D3 0 of 2 disagree, D4 0 of 2 disagree, D5 0 of 2 disagree and overall 0 of 2 disagree.9

That rate was measured before this review's D1 judgements moved. It is left as measured: On 2026-08-21 this review's D1 judgements moved from LOW to NO_INFORMATION on the RoB 2 guidance -- the position assessor 2 had taken. The rate above was measured before that and is left exactly as measured: it is a published number, it is the record of what a blind second assessor said, and it is the reason the guidance was re-read. Editing it would delete the evidence that the change was warranted. This is the same computation re-run on the object as it now stands, so both are visible and neither is silently corrected.10

Re-run on the object as it now stands: 2 of 12 judgements -- 16.7%. By domain: D1 2 of 2 disagree, D2 0 of 2 disagree, D3 0 of 2 disagree, D4 0 of 2 disagree, D5 0 of 2 disagree and overall 0 of 2 disagree.11

2 D1 judgement(s) on this topic moved. Any D1 disagreement that remains is one where this assessment said SOME_CONCERNS rather than LOW -- assessor 2 said NO_INFORMATION there too, and the guidance applied here speaks to LOW, not to SOME_CONCERNS. So a claim that 'the D1 disagreement is resolved' would be false wherever those two numbers differ, which is why the count is re-run per topic instead of asserted once.12

2 D1 disagreement(s) remain -- 2 where this assessment says NO_INFORMATION and assessor 2 says SOME_CONCERNS. Both assessors read the same absence of a concealment method, so this is a house-rule divergence and not an evidential one. RoB 2's algorithm answers some concerns when 1.2 is `No information` and there is no baseline concern; this project writes NO_INFORMATION on the domain instead, so a reader can tell a domain nobody could evaluate from a domain evaluated and found wanting. Both cap overall at the same place. The disagreement is real and it is about vocabulary.13

Class 94 records assessor 2 saying NO_INFORMATION on D1/D2/D3 `100 of 100`. Measured across all 23 topics now stored that is 239 of 243, and all four exceptions are D1=SOME_CONCERNS on `agyw-hiv-prep-review` and `cab-prep-hiv-review` -- two of the three topics asked under the earlier prompt build, the one whose reply ids are bare NCTs. Under that build it is 4 of 6; under the later build 0 of 75. The 100% was measured on the later build's topics. The two-defaults mechanism stands; its universality does not, and what varies with it is the prompt.14

Risk of bias was assessed independently a second time by GPT-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`, blind to this assessment and given the same registry facts. 2 of 12 judgements on this topic -- 16.7%. Both are D1 and nothing else. D2, D3, D4, D5 and the overall all agree. By domain: D1 2 of 2 disagree, D2 0 of 2 disagree, D3 0 of 2 disagree, D4 0 of 2 disagree, D5 0 of 2 disagree, overall 0 of 2 disagree. Recounted after this review's D1 judgements moved: 2 of 12 judgements -- 16.7%.15

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons..1

LOW certainty, and the reason is not the size of the effect -- which is large, consistent in direction, and reproduced exactly by a published synthesis. It is that two trials in two different populations across two regions have been combined into one ratio, with I-squared 68.83%, and that the adherence domain both trials turn on was not read.2

Certainty of the evidence, by outcome, with every rating step3
OutcomeCertaintykStarted atRating steps
documented incident HIV infectionLOW2risk of bias -- Both results are SOME_CONCERNS. Randomised, quadruple-masked including the outcomes assessor, single unambiguous efficacy primary -- but D2 and D3 are NO_INFORMATION, and the comparator arm here is a daily oral pill whose adherence is precisely what the unread domain would describe. (move: HIGH to MODERATE, down 1 level(s)); inconsistency -- tau-squared 0.4178, Q 3.2077 on 1 df, p = 0.0733, I-squared 68.83%. At k = 2 the statistic is weak evidence on its own, but it does not stand on its own here: The two trials are in different populations. 0.3335 (0.1785 to 0.6230) in men who have sex with men and transgender women, and 0.1108 (0.0395 to 0.3107) in cisgender women. A named reason for the spread is stronger than the statistic. (move: MODERATE to LOW, down 1 level(s)); indirectness -- the pool crosses both population and region. HPTN 084 ran in seven African countries in female participants. HPTN 083 ran in men who have sex with men and transgender women across Argentina, Brazil, Peru, South Africa, Thailand, the United States and Vietnam -- seven countries of which one is african -- and it is the larger and more precisely estimated of the two. A single ratio assembled across those two is not a quantity that answers either question cleanly. (move: LOW to very LOW, down 1 level(s)); imprecision -- k = 2. The Hartung-Knapp interval is RR 0.2081 (0.0002 to 212.2504) on t = 12.7062 with 1 df, which carries no information at all. The rating cannot fall below very LOW, so this domain is recorded as warranting a downgrade the scale cannot express. The unadjusted interval, 0.0715 to 0.6057, still excludes no difference by a wide margin. (move: Very LOW -- already at the floor, no further downgrade applied); publication bias -- k = 2. Handbook 13.3.5.4. (move: Not assessable -- no rating applied)

Discussion

[Draft] The pooled RR is 0.208 (95% CI 0.071 to 0.606) over 2 trials, against daily oral TDF/FTC. Certainty is rated LOW. Every contributing interval excludes no effect. Whether a change of that magnitude is clinically meaningful in this population is the author's judgement: no field on this object records a threshold of importance, and none is assumed here.1

[Draft] Across 2 trials, I-squared is 68.8%; tau-squared 0.4176; every trial interval excludes no effect. At k=2 these statistics are weak evidence about consistency in either direction. Two points cannot demonstrate agreement. Whether that degree of disagreement matters clinically -- whether the trials are answering the same question in the same patients -- is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] This review pools 0.208 (95% CI 0.071 to 0.606) over 2 trials. The appraised synthesis pooled HIV-1 infection under CAB-LA versus tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-emtricitabine, plus safety and treatment outcomes not comparable to this object over 10,957 participants. Which trials that synthesis carries: Not read. The abstract names none of its included studies, so which trials it carries is counted and not identified. But see the event counts below, which establish that the CAB-LA prevention contrast rests on the same events as ours. Why the two results differ -- whether by population, outcome definition, model or included set -- is the author's judgement.3

[Draft] The evidence base is 2 trials, assessed for risk of bias as SOME_CONCERNS on 2 result(s). GRADE certainty is LOW, rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness and imprecision. Whether that is enough to answer the question depends on the decision the answer is for, which is not stated on this object, and is the author's judgement.4

[Draft] primary trials. No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 2 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on 2026-08-18; Both registrations read on 2026-08-18: conditions, arm groups with types, registered primaries, posted results counts. Published syntheses. PubMed E-utilities esearch + esummary, executed 2026-08-21. Query as executed: (cabotegravir[tiab]) and (prophylaxis[tiab] OR PrEP[tiab] OR prevention[tiab]) and (meta-analysis[pt] OR "systematic review"[pt] OR meta-analysis[tiab] OR pooled[tiab]). It matched 46 record(s), of which 46 were retrieved and 46 read; 1 appraised. Whether that is broad enough for the claim this review makes is the author's judgement.5

[Draft] Certainty was rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness and imprecision. What further evidence would change the conclusion is a judgement about a trial nobody has run, and is the author's.6

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities esearch + esummary, executed 2026-08-21. Query, counts and per-record disposition in ssot/cab-prep-hiv-review/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json.1

This review was compared against 1 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

What this comparison found. The closest agreement with a published synthesis anywhere in this corpus. Wang et al., jmir Public Health and Surveillance 2023, PMID 37498645, report CAB-LA versus TDF/FTC for prevention as RR 0.21 (95% CI 0.07 to 0.61), I-squared 70%, on 17 events of 5,161 against 75 of 5,129. This object reports RR 0.2081 (0.0715 to 0.6057), I-squared 68.83%, on 13 + 4 = 17 events against 39 + 36 = 75. The event counts are the same numbers. The one place the two differ. They pool 5,161 and 5,129 participants; this object pools 3,894 and 3,891 -- about 1,250 more per arm on their side, contributing no events. Nothing read explains where those participants come from; the candidates are a wider analysis population on the same two trials, or a further prevention trial with zero infections. Which it is has not been established and no included-study table was opened. Their review states twelve trials -- seven of them prevention trials -- against this object's two. On the stated count alone that is the largest gap in the corpus. Yet the contrast itself rests on the same seventeen and seventy-five events. A stated trial count and the evidence contributing to a particular contrast are different things, and this topic is the proof. It is why class 82 reports 'ours lower' and 'trials identified' as separate states, and why the four count-only topics are worded as a difference in stated counts and nothing more. What the agreement does not certify is that the pool is a good idea. The two trials are in different populations across different regions and I-squared is 68.83%. A second team reaching the same number from the same events does not make the combination appropriate -- it makes the arithmetic checked. GRADE certainty here is LOW and indirectness is rated down.3

On what basis their trial set is known: Not read. The abstract names none of its included studies, so which trials it carries is counted and not identified. But see the event counts below, which establish that the CAB-LA prevention contrast rests on the same events as ours.4

Conclusions

[Draft] Across 2 randomised trials, RR was 0.208 (95% CI 0.071 to 0.606) for documented incident HIV infection against daily oral TDF/FTC. Certainty in that estimate is LOW. That is the estimate. What the evidence shows -- stated as a finding rather than as a number -- is the author's sentence.1

[Draft] What a clinician should do differently on this evidence -- the estimate and certainty stated above -- is a recommendation, not a measurement. No field on this object can back one, and none is drafted. It is the author's sentence.2

[Draft] What a payer, guideline or programme should do on this evidence -- the estimate and certainty stated above -- is a recommendation, not a measurement. No field on this object can back one, and none is drafted. It is the author's sentence.3
